topic: Canonical active-face certificates for exact-hit saturation-policy design. This is a new attempt at parent exp_saturation_exacthit_deficiency_design, not a retry of its nonmeasurable full-open-simplex scaffold. Fix K>=3, cluster size n0, distinct rational interior counts m_k, unrestricted binary within-cluster potential-outcome schedules, and exact-slice welfare U_k. Compare exact-count allocation a with nominal-label Bernoulli assignment p, whose exact-hit rates are q=Bp with B_kl=Pr{Bin(n0,m_l/n0)=m_k}. For each active face define the all-Borel randomized-selector Gaussian simple-regret value G_A(v,r), with singleton value zero and infinity at action-relevant zero information. Construct a terminating rational certificate that analytically prunes the exact-count boundary, partitions only closed positive-rate and covariance cells, returns outward epsilon brackets and all-minimizer cells for inf_a G_K(v,a) and inf_p G_K(v,Bp), and chooses lexicographically first designs only on an explicit finite certified grid. Realize every finite selector by a fixed inverse-CDF map jointly Borel in pilot covariance, screening and decision statistics, and an auxiliary uniform; covariance partitions apply only when |A|>=2. For primitive transfer, work at attainable binary full-tie baselines with v in a declared positive domain and O(C^-1/2) covariance neighborhoods, not exact membership in arbitrary singleton variance boxes. Prove a uniform calibrated three-way-split LAN risk sandwich over deterministic allocation sequences, including a vanishing-share converse and partial-tie subfaces. Return certified regret and cluster-count ratios; decide strict loss from the rational total-hit condition and provide finite certificates for positive excess over the mass floor, without claiming a total numerical equality oracle. Use the n0=6 menu m=(1,2,4), legal variance box [1/8,1/4]^3, and Egger et al.'s Kenya saturation design as the worked consumer. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The presolver derived G_K(v,a)>=kappa sqrt(v_i/a_i), giving the explicit uniform prune eta=1/1024 on [1/8,1/4]^3, and realized every variance there at a full tie using W in {0,1/2,1}. Ordered finite cells plus inverse-CDF weights give a canonical Borel evaluator. A vanishing allocation share makes local alternatives indistinguishable and forces divergent scaled regret. For the three-label menu on active face {1,2}, exact rational interval arithmetic gives p3*=0, p1*=0.289596897074... and regret ratio in [1.296043143254,1.296043143255]. Destructive checks rejected the parent's illegal [1,2]^3 binary witness, exact covariance membership in arbitrary V, global least-rational choices, and a purported total equality decision; the corrected statements preserve the model and target. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove the quantitatively uniform primitive risk sandwich for the finite canonical receipt family, combining calibrated ratio errors, screening tails, enlarged covariance cells, finite-prior uniform LAN, and one computable diagonal schedule. EARLY KILL TEST: Build a fixed-tolerance n0=6,K=3 receipt on [1/8,1/4]^3 with eta=1/1024, exact singleton branches, boundary-safe inverse-CDF decoding, a full-observation finite-prior lower bound, and independent-screen upper risk; reproduce the solved active-pair interval and one full-tie three-arm covariance before attempting the general theorem. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/exp_saturation_exacthit_canonical_activeface_certificate.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one construct a terminating rational, jointly Borel active-face receipt system for G_A that handles singleton faces exactly, partitions only closed positive-rate covariance cells, analytically prunes exact-count boundaries, and encloses every outer minimizer?

source_refs.claim: Characterizes multi-arm Gaussian minimax-regret rules with arbitrary covariance and proposes covariance plug-in asymptotics, but does not certify continua of design and covariance cells by exact rational arithmetic.
source_refs.author: Joonhwi Joo

source_refs.claim: Constructs convergent numerical minimax approximations by discretizing nature and using fictitious play, without a finite rational covariance-cell certificate or complete minimizer-cell output.
source_refs.author: Patrik Guggenberger and Jiaqi Huang

open_problems.why_unsolved: Published many-arm work supplies either asymptotic rules, convergent finite-game approximations, or covariance-indexed plug-in rules, but not finite termination with outward rounding over continuous allocation and covariance parameters. The parent run exposed the exact missing pieces: arbitrary covariance-cell choice made the selector potentially non-Borel, its covariance partition made singleton faces vacuous, and its transcript incorrectly tried to cover the entire open exact-count simplex with finitely many bounded cells. The first proof step must therefore replace arbitrary optimizer choice by an ordered finite cell decomposition and a fixed inverse-CDF realization, with quotient-tail control and analytic boundary coercivity before any numerical subdivision.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A terminating algorithm and correctness theorem returning outward rational brackets for every G_A cell, all cells containing global minimizers of the exact-count and Bp outer problems, exact singleton and zero-information branches, and a jointly Borel inverse-CDF selector on every retained closed cell.

writing_exemplar.why: Its one-shot multi-arm regret formulation most clearly separates the Gaussian decision problem from the experimental-design layer and exposes the covariance dependence the receipt must control.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A one-shot experiment must select one policy -> heteroskedastic Gaussian evidence makes empirical-best selection non-minimax -> least-favorable-prior rules solve compact instances -> exact-hit design needs a canonical certificate across active faces and boundaries.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its finite least-favorable-prior Gaussian selector and covariance plug-in risk comparison, replacing arbitrary rule selection by ordered finite cells and fixed inverse-CDF decoding.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It treats the same Gaussian best-arm regret functional on compact positive-covariance domains; the desired receipt adds noncompact quotient tails, active-face changes, exact singleton branches, and canonical measurability.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the reduction to finite zero-sum games and computable primal-dual risk bounds after discretizing nature, replacing limiting fictitious-play convergence by outward interval enclosures.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It attacks the same computational minimax bottleneck, while the target theorem must terminate finitely and certify every minimizing design cell over covariance uncertainty.

open_problems.open_problem: Does one computable three-way pilot-screen-decision split yield a uniform asymptotic minimax risk sandwich for canonical receipts over deterministic exact-count allocation sequences, including partial-tie subfaces and vanishing action-relevant shares?

source_refs.claim: Develops Gaussian limit-experiment approximations and asymptotic minimax treatment rules under smooth statistical models, not fixed-potential-outcome saturation randomization with changing active faces.
source_refs.author: Keisuke Hirano and Jack R. Porter

source_refs.claim: Derives large-sample randomization inference for direct and spillover estimators under partial interference and two-stage permutation randomization, without selector-indexed minimax risk transfer.
source_refs.author: Lan Liu and Michael G. Hudgens
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Provides randomization-based estimators, conservative variances, tests, and power formulas for vectors of exact-count assignment mechanisms while treating the design distribution as fixed.
source_refs.author: Zhichao Jiang, Kosuke Imai, and Anup Malani

source_refs.excerpt: The primitive LAN lower bounds are stated for fixed allocations
The fixed-count triangular array needs its own within-stratum pilot argument
Ordinary DQM or pointwise LAN does not imply the experiment-equivalence premise.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The Gaussian decision literature starts from smooth limit experiments, while two-stage interference papers establish CLTs and variance formulas for fixed estimators. Neither controls the risk of a finite family of pilot-selected, screened randomized selectors uniformly over shrinking covariance neighborhoods, deterministic allocation sequences, and all tie faces. The parent likewise proved only fixed-allocation LAN lower bounds and compact-positive-share transfer statements. The first missing step is a single quantitative comparison that simultaneously absorbs calibrated-ratio error, screening tails, covariance-cell enlargement, finite-prior likelihood convergence, and receipt tolerance on one computable diagonal; vanishing shares leave the positive-information experiment and need a separate indistinguishability converse.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A lower-and-upper theorem sandwiching scaled primitive simple regret by G_A(v,r) plus and minus an explicit o(1) under one computable split-and-mesh schedule, uniformly over declared positive covariance neighborhoods and deterministic allocations, with correct partial-tie restrictions and divergent risk for vanishing action-relevant shares.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates experiments whose design objective is welfare-optimal policy choice under spillovers, rather than effect estimation alone.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Interference changes policy welfare -> conventional designs target effect precision rather than the final decision -> pilot-informed design must control welfare loss -> prove a uniform exact-count minimax-regret guarantee for saturation choice.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt finite-prior local asymptotic minimax lower bounds and transfer of efficient statistics into Gaussian treatment rules to the exact-hit triangular array.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the canonical primitive-to-Gaussian decision-risk bridge; the strengthening is uniformity over receipt branches, deterministic allocations, and changing tie faces.

method_exemplars.technique: Use finite-population CLTs for two-stage permutation estimators as the primitive approximation before proving uniform integrability and selector-risk transfer.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its assignment-based asymptotics are the nearest route to controlling exact-count saturation statistics before upgrading pointwise CLTs to a uniform decision-risk sandwich.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent multiple saturation-specific potential outcomes as split-plot contrasts and derive their joint randomization covariance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target Gaussian vector is indexed by the same kind of exact-count saturation mechanisms, but the new proof must add calibration, screening, and minimax selector risk.

open_problems.open_problem: Can strict Bernoulli-label mechanism loss above the active-hit mass floor be decided by a rational total-hit condition and certified by a positive rational excess interval, without assuming a total numerical equality oracle for Gaussian risks?

source_refs.claim: Explicitly distinguishes fixed-proportion type-A assignment from independent-Bernoulli type-B assignment under interference, but studies effect partitioning rather than welfare-decision information loss.
source_refs.author: Tyler J. VanderWeele and Eric J. Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.claim: Optimizes randomized saturation designs for power, not the loss in Gaussian policy-selection information induced by the binomial exact-hit map B.
source_refs.author: Sarah Baird, J. Aislinn Bohren, Craig McIntosh, and Berk Özler

Solve these finitely many polynomial systems by exact real-algebraic elimination

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing interference-design papers recognize fixed-count and Bernoulli mechanisms but evaluate causal-effect estimators or power, not the exact-hit matrix as a decision-theoretic thinning of policy information. The parent proved a mass-floor inequality and an equality characterization but, outside its support-and-normalized-vector case, gave neither the exact general-K ratio nor a positive excess receipt. Exact algebraic branch enumeration works for the adjacent polynomial saturation program, but Gaussian selector risks contain normal integrals; the first changed step is to combine the rational total-hit equality branch with compactness, strict separation, and validated analytic risk enclosures rather than pretend that CAD or a numerical optimizer can decide arbitrary transcendental equality.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient comparison of inf_a G_K(v,a) and inf_p G_K(v,Bp) that proves equality from the rational total-hit condition when it holds and otherwise terminates with a rational delta>0 certifying Bernoulli regret at least the mass floor plus delta, including independently checkable optimizer and risk cells for n0=6 and m=(1,2,4).

writing_exemplar.why: It places fixed-count and Bernoulli second-stage mechanisms side by side, providing the cleanest narrative entry to exact-hit information loss.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Two-stage interference designs permit fixed-count or Bernoulli assignment -> the mechanisms support different causal summaries -> exact-slice welfare uses only realized target counts -> characterize and certify the resulting policy-selection loss.

method_exemplars.technique: Condition on the second-stage allocation strategy to isolate exact-count potential-outcome slices before expressing Bernoulli assignment as a known mixture over them.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The hit map B is obtained by precisely this conditioning, and the resulting slices define the common causal welfare target compared across mechanisms.

method_exemplars.technique: Use Gaussian limit-experiment risk comparison for randomized treatment rules under minimax welfare loss.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After the hit map changes information rates from a to Bp, the two optimized quantities are values of the same Gaussian minimax treatment-choice experiment.

method_exemplars.technique: Evaluate fixed allocations through least-favorable-prior Gaussian minimax regret and bound the value under covariance perturbations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The positive excess is a comparison of two attainable information regions under the same multi-arm Gaussian simple-regret functional.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the exact attainable covariance region of exact-slice welfare statistics at a common-welfare tie under unrestricted binary within-cluster potential-outcome schedules, and which positive covariance neighborhoods admit constructive realization on each active face?

source_refs.claim: Shows that finite-population randomization variances depend on unobserved joint potential-outcome covariance and derives sharp bounds from marginal outcome information.
source_refs.author: Peter M. Aronow, Donald P. Green, and Donald K. K. Lee

source_refs.claim: Derives optimal saturation designs under an imposed variance-covariance structure, making cluster-level covariance information a load-bearing design input.
source_refs.author: Sarah Baird, J. Aislinn Bohren, Craig McIntosh, and Berk Özler

source_refs.claim: Avoids imposing a potential-outcome covariance model but uses conservative randomization variances rather than characterizing realizable covariance inputs for welfare-optimal saturation design.
source_refs.author: Zhichao Jiang, Kosuke Imai, and Anup Malani

open_problems.why_unsolved: Sharp finite-population variance work optimizes the unobserved coupling of two marginal potential-outcome lists, whereas saturation-design papers either impose covariance structure or fall back to conservative bounds. Here several exact-slice averages are generated by one shared binary schedule, so their covariance coordinates cannot be selected independently and arbitrary singleton variance boxes need not be attainable. The first proof step must replace scalar rearrangement with a multi-marginal combinatorial characterization respecting slice incidence and the common-welfare tie; searches for attainable covariance matrices of exact-slice saturation welfare found no occupied target-method pair.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite semialgebraic or polyhedral characterization of all active-face covariance matrices attainable at binary full-tie baselines, plus an explicit schedule construction realizing a declared positive domain and uniform O(C^-1/2) neighborhoods of every covariance used by the primitive risk sandwich.

writing_exemplar.why: It makes covariance structure operational for saturation-design choice and explains why richer spillover comparisons trade off against precision.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Saturation variation identifies policy-relevant spillovers -> design precision depends on potential-outcome covariance -> unrestricted binary schedules constrain that covariance -> characterize the covariance inputs a regret-optimal design may legitimately use.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt sharp covariance bounds obtained by optimizing couplings of unobserved paired potential outcomes with fixed marginals to a multi-slice shared-schedule coupling.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both are attainable-set problems for unobserved finite-population dependence, but the target has several slice averages and a common-tie constraint rather than one two-arm scalar covariance.

method_exemplars.technique: Use vector finite-population central limit theorems for multiple treatments and cluster-randomized designs under assignment-only randomness.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once an attainable covariance neighborhood is constructed, the vector CLT is the natural route from those binary schedules to the Gaussian welfare statistics used by the receipt.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the split-plot linear-contrast representation of multiple saturation-specific potential outcomes and its randomization covariance formula.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its vector of exact-count saturation mechanisms supplies the covariance map whose feasible range must be characterized under one shared binary schedule.

literature_map:
Hudgens and Halloran (2008, JASA, DOI:10.1198/016214508000000292) established direct, indirect, total, and overall effects under two-stage partial-interference designs.
VanderWeele and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2011, Statistics & Probability Letters, DOI:10.1016/j.spl.2011.02.019) separated fixed-proportion type-A assignment from independent-Bernoulli type-B assignment, but only for effect partitioning.
Tchetgen Tchetgen and VanderWeele (2012, Statistical Methods in Medical Research, DOI:10.1177/0962280210386779) developed causal estimands and inference under interference, including exact-count strategies.
Liu and Hudgens (2014, JASA, DOI:10.1080/01621459.2013.844698) supplied large-sample randomization inference for two-stage permutation designs.
Basse and Feller (2018, JASA, arXiv:1608.06805) connected unbiased randomization inference and regression for two-stage experiments with exact within-household assignment.
Baird, Bohren, McIntosh, and Özler (2018, Review of Economics and Statistics, DOI:10.1162/rest_a_00716) optimized randomized saturation designs for power, not simple-regret information loss.
Jiang, Imai, and Malani (2023, Biometrics, DOI:10.1111/biom.13782) generalized inference and power analysis to multiple exact-count saturation mechanisms while holding their distribution fixed.
Egger, Haushofer, Miguel, Niehaus, and Walker (2022, Econometrica, DOI:10.3982/ECTA17945) used high/low geographic saturation in Kenya, providing the principal worked application.
Viviano (2019, arXiv:1906.10258) studied welfare under network interference; Viviano and Rudder (arXiv:2011.08174) designed experiments for welfare-optimal policies under unknown within-cluster interference.
Hirano and Porter (2009, Econometrica, DOI:10.3982/ECTA6630) developed Gaussian limit-experiment minimax treatment rules, but not fixed-potential-outcome saturation randomization.
Masten (2023, Japanese Economic Review, DOI:10.1007/s42973-023-00147-0) showed failures of empirical-success rules with many treatments and motivated computational game methods.
Guggenberger and Huang (2025, arXiv:2503.10932) gave convergent fictitious-play approximations, while Joo (2025, arXiv:2509.03796) treated multi-arm Gaussian minimax regret with arbitrary covariance; neither gives finite rational active-face receipts.
Aronow, Green, and Lee (2014, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1405.6555) and Li and Ding (2017, JASA, DOI:10.1080/01621459.2017.1295865) supply the closest sharp-covariance and vector finite-population-CLT machinery.
The unoccupied intersection is decision-optimal exact-count saturation design: exact-hit Bernoulli thinning, uniform assignment-based LAN risk over tie faces, binary-schedule covariance attainability, and canonical finite certification are not jointly addressed.
prior_proposal_map:
The bounded active/banked catalogue scan identified failed parent exp_saturation_exacthit_deficiency_design/v1 as the nearest source.
Its proto_core honest_scope isolates uniform face, covariance, and boundary certification as unresolved.
Its README records three concrete scaffold failures: nonmeasurable selector choice, vacuous singleton covariance cells, and impossible finite coverage of the open exact-count simplex.
Reviewer files angle0_v1, angle0_v2, and angle0_v3 were inspected; angle0_v3 adds data-driven allocation, heterogeneous-size, and reproducible three-policy-certificate directions.
The cold general review states two sharper gaps: no exact general-K ratio outside the equality case and no primitive optimized minimax identity uniform over allocation sequences.
F1.5 reviews were inspected and show that a pointwise finite-action Bayes lemma cannot simply be integrated into the observation-dependent Gaussian selector value.
Rejected angle0 of stat_nonsmooth_asymmetric_mmr_saddle/v2 supplies a compact measurable-rule exchange certificate but excludes the noncompact multi-action setting needed here.
Downgraded exp_saturation_skew_threshold/v1 supplies an exact algebraic saturation optimizer, clarifying why the exact-hit analogue needs validated Gaussian-risk enclosures rather than a total equality oracle.
Accepted exp_bipartite_minimax_design/v1 supplies a nearby observable design certificate, but its convex-envelope KKT proof does not directly cover nested exact-hit Gaussian regret.
